newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra unlikely to recoup rail network debt.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra unlikely to recoup rail network debt.

text.p: The Federal Government did not expect to recoup through the proposed sale of the Australian National (AN) rail network the A$2 billion cost of paying off AN's debts, Transport Minister John Sharp said on Wednesday.
"It does have a value...but I do not think we are going to recoup our A$2,000 million in the process," Sharp said in an interview on Adelaide radio station 5DN.
Sharp announced last Sunday that it planned to sell the debt-ridden rail business as part of a plan to revive the country's rail system and cut transport cost.

"Anybody taking over AN is going to be in for considerable capital investment and a considerably greater capital investment over the next few years to get it up to speed," Sharp said in the radio interview.

"We know that by putting it out to a competitive tendering process, such as we are, that we will get the best available price for it but at the same time we do not expect to get billions of dollars for AN," he said.
Sharp said a number of Australian owned companies had expressed interest in AN's assets, and confirmed that Macquarie Bank Ltd had shown interest in buying all of AN.
"Certainly Macquarie Bank has been around, they have spoken to the Public Transport Union, the South Australian government, they have addressed our rail reform committee in Canberra," Sharp said.
"Macquarie Bank..certainly have indicated they want to buy all of AN," he said.
